sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible degree route: UChicago bachelor's before enrollment; F1 does not exclude international admission.
MATH expects real analysis, theoretical linear algebra and abstract algebra. FAQ says GPA should exceed 3.0;
actual GPA/preparation are unknown, so individual eligibility remains conditional. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select MATH, not STAT/AMSC; choose one or two research areas rather than 'undecided' (not binding). Prepare
course supplement, transcripts, CV, statements and three referees. Resolve conflicting English-waiver
instructions before relying on UChicago. Start a fee-waiver request before paying/submitting. No advance
supervisor consent stated. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s9] [s17]

No advance sponsorship requirement. Current faculty below; read papers before contact and confirm
availability. Emeritus/research positions marked. Admissions contact: math-grads@umd.edu. [s1] [s2] [s20] [s21]

requests. Send official tests centrally. Submitted applications generally are not editable; department updates
are discretionary. Inspect document rendering and letter receipt. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Admission and TA certification differ. New TOEFL speaking 5 / IELTS speaking 7.5 avoids the TA English class;
4.5 / 7 requires class. Writing 5 / IELTS 7 avoids the writing course; reading/listening 5 / IELTS 7 are relevant
minima. Central overall TOEFL 5 / IELTS 7. Legacy MATH PTE speaking 76 and central PTE overall 68 measure
different things. Confirm the test/date-specific table and department waiver; admission exemption alone does
not establish TA eligibility. [s1] [s2] [s9]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
CONFLICT: the central qualifying-US-degree exemption permits a degree completed or expected by enrollment,
with in-country study; online/branch study is excluded and transfer/dual routes need at least two years in an
eligible country. A full on-campus UChicago bachelor's appears centrally eligible (inference). The MATH catalog
nevertheless requires TOEFL/IELTS even for otherwise exempt applicants; the main page uses no-exceptions
language. FAQ describes a US master's waiver but does not resolve bachelor's eligibility. Obtain a written
MATH ruling. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s9]
GRE General [Conflict]
Current admissions: optional. FAQ strongly encourages scores after the pandemic policy. A legacy
educational-policy page still says required; the current optional admissions rule takes precedence, with the
conflict preserved. [s1] [s2] [s16]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Optional, strongly recommended; FAQ advises submitting scores above 700 and prioritizing Math Subject if
taking one. Legacy 'required' wording is stale. This is not a 'not considered' policy. [s1] [s2] [s16]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
MATH FAQ historical 2024 base: $28,311 plus a usual $5,000 in each of the first two years = $33,311, NOT a
2027 amount. FY27 central full doctoral precandidacy minimum: $29,023 over 9.5 months or $36,660 over 12
months (2026-27), not a Fall 2027 departmental guarantee. Do not add the historical supplement to the newer
minimum or assume summer coverage. [s2] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally five years, sometimes six, subject to progress and departmental conditions; the sixth year is not
unconditional. Median completion time of 5.5 years is descriptive, not a funding entitlement. [s2] [s16]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary TA funding is available to international PhD students; the department supports accepted students
except some employer-funded cases. Federal citizenship-restricted awards are separate. A 9.5-month salary
and 12-month visa financial requirement may differ; assistantships are not ordinarily performed abroad. [s2]
[s11] [s14] [s15]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Progress and duties required. Central full assistantship: 20 hours/week; MATH estimates 4-6 contact hours and
12-15 total hours for common assignments. Tuition up to 10 credits/semester; fees and exact health premium
are separate. English-cost conflict: the central English page says uncovered, while newer GA tuition rules allow
UMEI 506/507 from Fall 2025 and MATH retains UMEI 007 wording. Confirm current course/cost/coverage; the
historical 2023 English cost of $3,083 is not current. [s2] [s9] [s13] [s14] [s15]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
Ordinary TA review accompanies admission; separate fellowships may require nomination. A universal extra
form/essay is not established. Department fee-waiver request emailed by December 1. [s1] [s2] [s14]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Conditional summer teaching/research, adviser grants, campus assistantships through Workday/Resident Life,
and department/Graduate School fellowships. No universal summer guarantee. [s2] [s14]
Application fee [Conflict]
Current central fee: $90 per program, online before processing, nonrefundable. MATH's $75 is older/conflicting.
Budget $90 and verify the portal. [s1] [s6] [s17]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Fall 2027 MATH: email math-grads@umd.edu by December 1, 2026 with subject 'Fee Waiver Request- Your

Last Name' and attach a transcript; CV, paper and reference optional. A handful are awarded in early
December. Central qualifying preparatory-program waivers take 10-15 business days; request at least three
weeks before the deadline. Start the application but do not submit/pay until approved. Domestic FreeApp does
not automatically cover F1 applicants; no refund. [s2] [s17]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible degree route: UChicago bachelor's before enrollment; F1 does not exclude international admission.
MATH expects real analysis, theoretical linear algebra and abstract algebra. FAQ says GPA should exceed 3.0;
actual GPA/preparation are unknown, so individual eligibility remains conditional. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select MATH, not STAT/AMSC; choose one or two research areas rather than 'undecided' (not binding). Prepare
course supplement, transcripts, CV, statements and three referees. Resolve conflicting English-waiver
instructions before relying on UChicago. Start a fee-waiver request before paying/submitting. No advance
supervisor consent stated. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s9] [s17]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance sponsorship requirement. Current faculty below; read papers before contact and confirm
availability. Emeritus/research positions marked. Admissions contact: math-grads@umd.edu. [s1] [s2] [s20] [s21]

TerpEngage: select MATH, upload CV, statements, transcripts and course supplement, add referees and send
requests. Send official tests centrally. Submitted applications generally are not editable; department updates
are discretionary. Inspect document rendering and letter receipt. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]

English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Admission and TA certification differ. New TOEFL speaking 5 / IELTS speaking 7.5 avoids the TA English class;
4.5 / 7 requires class. Writing 5 / IELTS 7 avoids the writing course; reading/listening 5 / IELTS 7 are relevant
minima. Central overall TOEFL 5 / IELTS 7. Legacy MATH PTE speaking 76 and central PTE overall 68 measure
different things. Confirm the test/date-specific table and department waiver; admission exemption alone does
not establish TA eligibility. [s1] [s2] [s9]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
CONFLICT: the central qualifying-US-degree exemption permits a degree completed or expected by enrollment,
with in-country study; online/branch study is excluded and transfer/dual routes need at least two years in an
eligible country. A full on-campus UChicago bachelor's appears centrally eligible (inference). The MATH catalog
nevertheless requires TOEFL/IELTS even for otherwise exempt applicants; the main page uses no-exceptions
language. FAQ describes a US master's waiver but does not resolve bachelor's eligibility. Obtain a written
MATH ruling. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s9]
GRE General [Conflict]
Current admissions: optional. FAQ strongly encourages scores after the pandemic policy. A legacy
educational-policy page still says required; the current optional admissions rule takes precedence, with the
conflict preserved. [s1] [s2] [s16]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Optional, strongly recommended; FAQ advises submitting scores above 700 and prioritizing Math Subject if
taking one. Legacy 'required' wording is stale. This is not a 'not considered' policy. [s1] [s2] [s16]

renders blank, print and scan legibly. [s6] [s7]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
MATH FAQ historical 2024 base: $28,311 plus a usual $5,000 in each of the first two years = $33,311, NOT a
2027 amount. FY27 central full doctoral precandidacy minimum: $29,023 over 9.5 months or $36,660 over 12
months (2026-27), not a Fall 2027 departmental guarantee. Do not add the historical supplement to the newer
minimum or assume summer coverage. [s2] [s11]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally five years, sometimes six, subject to progress and departmental conditions; the sixth year is not
unconditional. Median completion time of 5.5 years is descriptive, not a funding entitlement. [s2] [s16]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary TA funding is available to international PhD students; the department supports accepted students
except some employer-funded cases. Federal citizenship-restricted awards are separate. A 9.5-month salary
and 12-month visa financial requirement may differ; assistantships are not ordinarily performed abroad. [s2]
[s11] [s14] [s15]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Progress and duties required. Central full assistantship: 20 hours/week; MATH estimates 4-6 contact hours and
12-15 total hours for common assignments. Tuition up to 10 credits/semester; fees and exact health premium
are separate. English-cost conflict: the central English page says uncovered, while newer GA tuition rules allow
UMEI 506/507 from Fall 2025 and MATH retains UMEI 007 wording. Confirm current course/cost/coverage; the
historical 2023 English cost of $3,083 is not current. [s2] [s9] [s13] [s14] [s15]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
Ordinary TA review accompanies admission; separate fellowships may require nomination. A universal extra
form/essay is not established. Department fee-waiver request emailed by December 1. [s1] [s2] [s14]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Conditional summer teaching/research, adviser grants, campus assistantships through Workday/Resident Life,
and department/Graduate School fellowships. No universal summer guarantee. [s2] [s14]

Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]

are discretionary. Inspect document rendering and letter receipt. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]

MATH FAQ historical 2024 base: $28,311 plus a usual $5,000 in each of the first two years = $33,311, NOT a

Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally five years, sometimes six, subject to progress and departmental conditions; the sixth year is not
unconditional. Median completion time of 5.5 years is descriptive, not a funding entitlement. [s2] [s16]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Ordinary TA funding is available to international PhD students; the department supports accepted students
except some employer-funded cases. Federal citizenship-restricted awards are separate. A 9.5-month salary

Conditional summer teaching/research, adviser grants, campus assistantships through Workday/Resident Life,
